source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect raw data: Gather all the relevant monitoring data from the air quality sensors and equipment used for measuring industrial emissions. This could include information on sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and any other relevant pollutants.

3. Identify monitoring methods: Give details on the techniques and technologies used for monitoring, such as continuous emissions monitoring systems (CEMS), non-destructive testing tools, satellite imagery, or periodic manual sampling.

4. Time period and frequency: Specify the time period over which the measurements were recorded, including start and end dates. Note down the frequency of the monitoring activities (e.g. hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or event-based).

5. Exceedance Thresholds: Define the regulatory standards for each pollutant, as set by the local, national, or international environmental agencies.
